title: Schematic generic density and fibre properties of the smooth open
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite type, flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Assume $Y$ is irreducible with generic point $\eta$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point] and $X_\eta$ is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(\eta)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Define $U\subseteq X$ to be the union of all open subschemes $T\subseteq X$ on which $f|_T$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $U_\eta$ is topologically dense in $X_\eta$ and, for its open immersion $j_\eta$, the natural sheaf map $\mathcal O_{X_\eta}\to(j_\eta)_*\mathcal O_{U_\eta}$ is injective. For every $y\in Y$, $X_y$ is a finite type $\kappa(y)$-scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian, meaning that every descending sequence of closed subsets stabilizes; every open immersion into $X_y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. For every $y\in Y$, $U_y$ is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(y)$. Empty fibres are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0578, lemma-geometrically-reduced-generic-fibre, second proof paragraph through the assertion that all fibres of the smooth open are geometrically reduced; varieties.tex Tag 056V, lemma-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open; morphisms.tex Tags 01V9 (lemma-smooth-at-point) and 056D (lemma-reduced-scheme-theoretically-dense)

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$. Base change of the finite-type morphism $f$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)\to Y$ gives a finite-type morphism $h_y:X_y\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal; hence its one-point spectrum is Noetherian. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X_y$ Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], closed subsets satisfy the minimal condition, so any descending sequence stabilizes: choose a minimal member among its terms. Every open immersion into $X_y$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc] and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation](a), hence quasi-separated: its diagonal is a closed immersion, which is quasi-compact since inverse images of affine opens are affine closed subschemes. Finally [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] makes $h_y$ locally finitely presented. These facts apply also to $y=\eta$.

source.place: Tag 0578, proof, finite-type fibres; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6; Properties Tag 01OY; Schemes Tag 01L7

proof.text: The open subschemes $T$ in the definition of $U$ cover $U$. Restricting $f|_T$ to its open domain inside $U$ gives exactly the restrictions of $f|_U$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] shows that $f|_U:U\to Y$ is smooth. This also covers $U=\varnothing$.

Apply [lem-pur-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open] to $h_\eta:X_\eta\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$: its local finite presentation was proved in step 1, and geometric reducedness is a hypothesis. Its smooth locus $V$ is dense in $X_\eta$. For each $w\in V$, [lem-trf-flat-fibre-smooth-locus-image] applies to $f$, since $f$ is flat and locally finitely presented. It gives an open neighbourhood of the image of $w$ on which $f$ is smooth. That image therefore lies in the union $U$. Consequently $V\subseteq U_\eta$, so $U_\eta$ is dense in $X_\eta$.

source.place: Tag 0578, proof, dense smooth generic open; varieties.tex Tag 056V (lemma-geometrically-reduced-dense-smooth-open); morphisms.tex Tag 01V9 (lemma-smooth-at-point)

proof.text: Geometric reducedness of $X_\eta$ implies reducedness by taking the identity field extension in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The open immersion $j_\eta:U_\eta\hookrightarrow X_\eta$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by step 1 and has dense image by step 3. Therefore [lemma-nagata-reduced-dense-image-schematic] says that its scheme-theoretic image inclusion is an isomorphism. The injectivity assertion of [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc], applied to this quasi-compact map, now gives $\mathcal O_{X_\eta}\to(j_\eta)_*\mathcal O_{U_\eta}$ injective after identifying the scheme-theoretic image with $X_\eta$. This is precisely schematic density as defined in [def-trf-schematically-dense-open].

source.place: Tag 0578, proof, schematic density; morphisms.tex Tag 056D (lemma-reduced-scheme-theoretically-dense)

proof.text: Apply [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] to the smooth morphism $f|_U$ from step 2. It gives geometric reducedness of its fibre $U_y$ for every $y\in Y$. An empty fibre is reduced after every field extension, and density and the sheaf injection over an empty generic fibre are vacuous, so none of the preceding steps requires nonempty fibres.
